headline: Inferring kinetics and time labels from nascent RNA and expression compendia
label: Temporal Inference In Transcriptomics
summary: Nascent RNA and archived expression data now support inference of kinetic parameters and time annotations without direct time measurements.
synthesis: The dominant thread is inference of time-linked quantities that the readout does not directly report. A moments-based framework applied to nascent RNA data derives closed-form moment expressions for transcriptional kinetics, with model selection validated within the framework. A supervised Bayesian method re-annotates time labels in transcriptomics experiments, addressing a related gap using existing expression data. The remaining items are compendium-scale resources: GEAR integrates legacy microarray and RNA-seq Arabidopsis data across 83 conditions, YeastCoDEGNet builds a co-differential expression network from 143 yeast microarray experiments, and GRAsp derives a regulatory network from 18 A. fumigatus RNA-seq datasets. These resources do not infer time directly, so temporal inference is shared only partly across the set. What is new is recovery of kinetic parameters from nascent RNA and of temporal labels from existing expression data.
